name: Vinaceous-Fawn
lede: Vinaceous-Fawn is a muted pink-brown, a paler cousin of Vinaceous-Cinnamon in Robert Ridgway's 1912 "vinaceous" family of wine-tinged naturalist colors.

sections.title: A fawn with a wine cast
sections.body:
Ridgway plated this hue in 1912 at plate XL, hue 13''', tone b, with no earlier 1886 record in our sources [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[japan-rose]], [[light-russet-vinaceous]] and [[beige-red]], at 3.5, 
In our library it is an exact color match to [[fawn]] itself (CIEDE2000 0.0), with two paler children of its own, [[light-vinaceous-fawn]] and [[pale-vinaceous-fawn]] [2]. Its nearest distinct neighbor is [[japan-rose]], almost the same at a distance of 3.5 [2]. Measured in LCH it is lightness 65, chroma 22 and hue 53 degrees, a little pinker and less saturated than Vinaceous-Cinnamon [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink-brown in 607 of 23,781 paintings (2.55%, as photographed), more common than 77% of the named colors we track [3]. It most often plays a light, in 38% of its 325 strongest matches [3]. Peter Paul Rubens is its most devoted painter, at 4.2 times the baseline rate across his 46 works here [3]. It is also most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.2 times the expected rate [3]. The earliest dated match runs to 1230, nearly seven centuries before Ridgway's 1912 record; the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the pigment was there, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
